subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Last year art critics praised Animesh as if he were a master, but he turned out to be __a pleasure for a short time. __

options.text: a bull in a china shop

solution: The correct answer is **Option 4)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The phrase **"a nine days’ wonder"** means something or someone** that creates a short-lived sensation or interest.** (अल्पकालिक चमत्कार) • **Example:** The new movie was a nine days' wonder, quickly forgotten after its initial success. • **Explanation:** The idiomatic expression "a nine days’ wonder" accurately describes something that is briefly popular or exciting but soon loses its appeal. (अल्पकालिक चमत्कार) • **Example:** The singer's sudden rise to fame was a **nine days’ wonder;** now, nobody remembers his name. Therefore, the correct idiom for the given phrase is **a nine days’ wonder**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **a house of cards** (ताश के पत्तों का महल): Something that is insubstantial or in danger of collapsing. • **Example:** The company's business model was **a house of cards**, easily falling apart when the market changed. • **a bull in a china shop** (चाइना की दुकान में सांड): Someone who is clumsy in a situation requiring delicacy. • **Example:** John is like **a bull in a china shop,** breaking everything in sight whenever he visits. • **a dish fit for Gods** (देवताओं के लिए उपयुक्त व्यंजन): Something that is of the highest quality. • **Example:** The chef prepared a meal that was truly** a dish fit for Gods**, impressing all the guests. 42:Tc8f, The correct answer is **Option 4)**
